metadata.title: Claude's SEC Filings Skill: Reliable, Not All-Knowing
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: once Claude has a skill file for SEC data, does it now generally understand finance, or only the specific things the file lists? Lands the carry-out that a skill file makes Claude's actions repeatable, not all-knowing. Redo of the cwc-workshops Teardown skill-teardown cut, same skill/facts, judgment removed.
metadata.anchor_pair: S03 -> S08 (must be the SAME case: the four-item spec list - company lookup, filings, XBRL statements, Item 1A risk factors)
metadata.one_flag: none needed - all claims restate the source SKILL.md's own scope description, not this reel's inference

beats.narration_text: A newcomer might think adding a skill means Claude now understands finance in general. It doesn't — it follows the file. So what does a skill file actually let Claude do?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive claim, hesitates on 'understands finance', corrects to 'follows the file', lands the real question

props.text:
Claude's SEC skill means it knows finance now?
What does it actually do?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md. Narration is 30 words, actual_duration_s 9.98s. Text/params tuned short and fast (charMs 45, hesitateBetween 10) after discovering the sibling reel's B00 (cwc-workshops--agent-decomposition-skills-vs-tools) never actually completes its own correction within its audio window -- verify media/B00.mp4 by pulling a frame at t=actual_duration_s-0.2 and confirming the 'the file' replacement AND the second line are both fully typed before compiling further.

beats.narration_text: Ask Claude to pull data from a company's SEC filings, and it reaches for a skill built for exactly that — a folder called edgartools-sec-data.

shot.new_visual_element: A request, and a folder that answers it

production_viz.label: A request, and a folder that answers it
production_viz.mechanic: A speech-bubble request ('pull SEC filing data') on the left. An arrow to a folder icon labelled edgartools-sec-data on the right.

beats.narration_text: The natural read: give Claude a skill for SEC data, and it must now generally understand finance and filings — ask it anything, and it'll know.

production_viz.label: The general-expertise reading
production_viz.mechanic: The folder icon glows and expands into a halo labelled 'FINANCE EXPERT', with arrows fanning out to many unrelated question marks. Sell the reading as reasonable.

beats.narration_text: Hold on to what the file actually says: company lookups, filings, XBRL financial statements, and sections like Item 1A risk factors. That's the whole list.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the four-item spec list

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — the four-item spec list
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four items listed top to bottom in serif on cream, each with a small teal check mark as it's named: company lookup, filings, XBRL financial statements, Item 1A risk factors. A bracket closes under the list: 'THE WHOLE LIST.' THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S08.

beats.narration_text: Ask for something off that list — say, whether the filing looks risky to you — and there's no step for it. The file never wrote that down.

production_viz.label: Off the list, nothing happens
production_viz.mechanic: The FINANCE EXPERT halo from S02 is struck through in crimson. A new question ('is this risky?') arrives at the folder and bounces back unanswered — no step lights up.

beats.narration_text: A skill is just a folder Claude reads before it acts. Here, one file does the job: SKILL.md — plain language, the whole instruction set, no hidden logic.

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens to reveal a single file card: SKILL.md, labelled 'the whole instruction set — plain language.' Nothing else is inside.

beats.narration_text: Claude reads the file, then works through its steps in order — read, then execute, then hand back the result. Linear, unless a step says otherwise.

production_viz.label: The pipeline: read, execute, return
production_viz.mechanic: Three boxes left to right — Read SKILL.md, Execute steps, Return result — connected by a single straight arrow. No branches.

beats.narration_text: That's what makes it repeatable: the same request runs the same steps, and produces the same kind of output, every single time.

shot.new_visual_element: Same request, same output, three times

production_viz.label: Same request, same output, three times
production_viz.mechanic: The S06 pipeline runs three times in a row, compressed; each run produces an identical output card. Teal check marks stack up.

beats.narration_text: Back to that list: ask for a company lookup or an XBRL statement, and you get the same reliable pull, every time. Ask outside it, and nothing happens — that step was never written.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — on the list vs. off it

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — on the list vs. off it
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 LIST COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical. A request for 'company lookup' checks against the list — teal match, reliable pull. A second request ('is this risky?') checks against the same list — no match, crimson bounce-back.

beats.narration_text: So the skill is dependable exactly when your question matches the file — a lookup, a filing, a financial statement.

production_viz.label: Matches the file: dependable
production_viz.mechanic: A question card slots cleanly into a file-shaped outline — a match — with a teal 'DEPENDABLE' stamp.

beats.narration_text: It flips the moment your question needs judgment the file doesn't have — asking whether a company looks like a good bet was never written into these steps.

shot.new_visual_element: Mirroring S09: needs judgment, no match

production_viz.label: Mirroring S09: needs judgment, no match
production_viz.mechanic: Mirroring S09's layout: a differently-shaped question card ('good bet?') fails to slot into the same file-shaped outline — crimson 'NOT WRITTEN IN' stamp.

beats.narration_text: A skill file makes Claude's actions repeatable, not all-knowing — it only does what the file actually wrote down.

props.quote: A skill file makes Claude's actions repeatable, not all-knowing — it only does what the file actually wrote down.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me: "Read the edgartools-sec-data skill, and list, in your own words, exactly which four things it lets you pull from SEC filings — then tell me one thing about a company you might want to know that isn't on that list." Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Read the edgartools-sec-data skill, and list, in your own words, exactly which four things it lets you pull from SEC filings — then tell me one thing about a company you might want to know that isn't on that list.
